# Dr. Anne Metz — Therapy for Women in New Mexico; Legal Psilocybin Facilitation in Colorado

> Dr. Anne Metz, PhD, LPC, is a licensed professional counselor based in New Mexico who provides legal psilocybin facilitation in Colorado (Colorado Natural Medicine Facilitator in Training, License No. NMIT.0000254). She does not hold a New Mexico psilocybin license. She specializes in legal psilocybin facilitation for women navigating perimenopause, menopause, infertility and reproductive grief, identity questions, and major life transitions. Medicine sessions take place at Numia Healing Center in Denver under Colorado's regulated Natural Medicine Program (Proposition 122, passed 2022). Preparation and integration sessions are available to anyone via telehealth.

## Key facts

- Practitioner: Dr. Anne Metz, PhD in Counselor Education & Supervision (James Madison University), Licensed Professional Counselor
- Licensed in Colorado, New Mexico, Oregon, California, and Virginia; Colorado Natural Medicine Facilitator in Training, License No. NMIT.0000254
- Director of Fluence Training's natural medicine program in Colorado; member of New Mexico's Medical Psilocybin Patient Safety Subcommittee; host of The Psychedelic Skeptic podcast
- Services: legal psilocybin facilitation for women (in person in Denver, Colorado; Taos, New Mexico expected January 2027 for people with a qualifying diagnosis); individual therapy for women via telehealth (CO, NM, OR, CA, VA); standalone psilocybin preparation and integration sessions (telehealth, available anywhere)
- A full course of facilitation includes five sessions: two preparation sessions, one full-day medicine session at Numia Healing Center in Denver, and two integration sessions; pricing starts at $3,800 including healing center access
- Pricing listed on partner organizations' sites (such as Odyssey PBC) reflects those organizations' own fees for their services, not Dr. Metz's direct practice pricing
- Insurance is not accepted for facilitation services
- Psilocybin facilitation in Colorado requires an in-person visit to Denver for the medicine session; clients travel from anywhere. Denver sessions continue after New Mexico's program begins
- New Mexico's Medical Psilocybin Program is expected to begin in January 2027; Dr. Metz plans to offer treatment in Taos once licensed
- New Mexico's program is medical: every participant needs a qualifying diagnosis (treatment-resistant depression, substance use disorder including cannabis or nicotine use disorders, PTSD, or end-of-life care) and a telehealth evaluation; a second staff member may be required during the medicine session; New Mexico pricing will be set once the rules are final and may be higher than Colorado; superbills planned for out-of-network commercial insurance, with the intake evaluation, preparation, and integration sessions coded as medically necessary health care appointments; Taos Regional Airport has direct flights from Denver year-round and from Austin, Dallas, and Carlsbad, California, in winter and summer; Taos setting: Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Carson National Forest, and Rio Grande Gorge, dark night skies (Taos is seeking Dark Sky certification), a small and quiet town with a long spiritual history (Taos Pueblo), and nearby skiing, hiking, rafting, and hot springs — details at https://annemetz.com/new-mexico.html
- Psilocybin facilitation is legal in Colorado under the state-regulated Natural Medicine Program — supervised therapeutic use, not recreational legalization
- Free 15-minute consultations offered; contact hello@annemetz.com or (720) 248-7368
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/annemetz/

- Psilocybin is not appropriate for everyone; contraindications include personal or family history of psychosis or schizophrenia spectrum disorders and certain medications such as lithium
